text: Everest (Mount Everest) is an 8000-metre-class mountain at 8848 m, located in Nepal / China (Tibet) in the Khumbu Himal. The first ascent was on 29.05.1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay. Principal routes include South Col–Southeast Ridge; North Col–Northeast Ridge. Base-camp context: South Base Camp / North Base Camp. High-camp context: South Col route: Camp 1, Camp 2, Camp 3, South Col; North route: North Col and higher camps. Major ridges and faces include Southeast Ridge; Northeast Ridge; West Face; Southwest Face; North Face. Important glacier/col terrain includes Khumbu Icefall; Western Cwm; South Col; North Col. Key technical characteristics include High-altitude exposure, steep snow/ice, fixed ropes, icefall and summit-ridge terrain. Typical environmental conditions include High winds, severe cold, jet-stream exposure and short weather windows near the summit. Major mountaineering hazards include Avalanche and serac/icefall hazards, falls, storms, hypoxia, frostbite and altitude illness.

text: K2 (K2 / Chogori) is an 8000-metre-class mountain at 8611 m, located in Pakistan / China in the Baltoro Muztagh, Karakoram. The first ascent was on 31.07.1954, Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli. Principal routes include Southeast Ridge (Abruzzi Spur); North Ridge; other major face/ridge routes. Base-camp context: K2 Base Camp. High-camp context: Advanced/high camps on the Abruzzi Spur, including Camp I–IV in common expedition descriptions. Major ridges and faces include Abruzzi Spur; North Ridge; South/Southwest faces; Bottleneck area on the Abruzzi route. Important glacier/col terrain includes Baltoro Glacier approach; Godwin-Austen Glacier area; high couloirs and seracs. Key technical characteristics include Steep rock, snow and ice; sustained mixed climbing; exposed fixed-rope terrain and complex summit-section climbing. Typical environmental conditions include Rapidly changing Karakoram weather, strong winds, extreme cold and narrow summit windows. Major mountaineering hazards include Avalanches, serac fall, rockfall, falls on steep terrain, storms, hypoxia and extreme exposure.
